new_results: For an exact-rank-three spectral frame U, Pluecker weights w_I=det(U_I)^2 form a probability law whose one-point marginals are the row leverages ell_i.
If R(U) is the probability that two independent Pluecker-volume sampled triples are disjoint, then R(U)>=1-sum_i ell_i^2.
For a fair random original-coordinate cut S, E[det(U_S^TU_S)det(U_{S^c}^TU_{S^c})]=R(U)/64.
Therefore if kappa=1-sum_i ell_i^2>0, some deterministic original-coordinate partition has rank-three cross-block singular-product Delta>=|det Lambda|sqrt(kappa)/8.
Applying the completed cross-block Fourier theorem gives ||p_Q||_infinity<=12|det Lambda|^(-1/3)kappa^(-1/6); under |lambda_j|>=1 this is <=12kappa^(-1/6).
If max row leverage is eta<1/3, the bound becomes 12(1-3eta)^(-1/6), extending the direct random-cut Fourier branch beyond the earlier 1/12 leverage certificate.
On the account02/B03 overlap-collapse family, R(U)=a^2 epsilon^2/2 and the best balanced cut has Delta=a epsilon/4, exactly exposing the necessary heavy-overlap fallback.
